back: $|x| = x$ if $x \geq 0$ and $|x| = -x$ if $x < 0$; it is the distance of $x$ from 0.

front: Shape and key points of $y = |ax + b|$
back: A V shape with vertex $\left(-\frac{b}{a}, 0\right)$, $y$-intercept $|b|$, arms of gradient $\pm a$.
$a - b < x < a + b$: one interval, centre $a$.
$x < a - b$ or $x > a + b$: two separate intervals.

front: When is it safe to square a modulus equation?
back: When both sides are non-negative (e.g. a modulus on each side). Otherwise use cases and check each answer.
Write $-(x + 4) < 2x - 1 < x + 4$ and solve both parts, or sketch the V and the line and read off where the line is above.
$|a + b| \leq |a| + |b|$, with equality when $a$ and $b$ have the same sign (or one is 0).
